questions.question: A business cycle is best defined as:
options: The successive periods of expansion and contraction in real economic activity around a long-term growth trend
Any rise in prices over time
The annual budget cycle of government

questions.question: The four phases of the cycle in correct order, starting from the lowest point, are:
The AMPLITUDE of a business cycle is:
options: The time from one peak to the next peak
The slope of the trend line
The vertical distance between the trend line and a peak or trough — a measure of the cycle's intensity
The number of quarters of negative growth

questions.question: A recession is conventionally declared after:
options: One month of falling share prices
A rise in the repo rate
Two consecutive quarters of falling real GDP

subtopics.title: Why Cycles Happen — Causes and Types

questions.question: EXOGENOUS explanations of the cycle locate its causes:
options: Outside the market system — weather, wars, oil shocks, pandemics and policy mistakes
Inside the market system, in confidence and investment swings
Only in the behaviour of trade unions

questions.question: The Keynesian view holds that:
options: Markets are self-correcting and government causes cycles
Markets are inherently unstable — confidence, the multiplier and the accelerator make swings feed themselves, so government must intervene
Cycles are caused only by sunspots and weather
The money supply should grow at a fixed rate

questions.question: Monetarists conclude that the best policy response to cycles is:
options: Stable, predictable policy — because markets self-correct and intervention itself causes the swings

questions.question: Match the cycle to its driver: the Kitchin, Juglar, Kuznets and Kondratieff cycles are driven respectively by:
options: Inventories, machinery investment, building and construction, technological revolutions

subtopics.title: Leaning Against the Wave — Monetary and Fiscal Policy

questions.question: The SARB's main monetary policy instrument is:
options: The repo rate — the rate at which it lends to commercial banks

questions.question: In the 2020 downswing the SARB cut the repo rate to 3,5 percent. This was:
options: Expansionary monetary policy — cheaper credit to support spending through the trough

questions.question: Automatic stabilisers dampen the cycle because:
options: Parliament votes on them every month
They only operate at the peak
Progressive tax takes less as incomes fall and grants and UIF pay out more as jobs are lost — with no new decision needed
They raise the repo rate automatically

questions.question: A key limit of both monetary and fiscal policy is that:
options: They only work in an upswing
They affect only the foreign sector
They act with lags, so badly timed policy can amplify the very wave it was meant to flatten

subtopics.title: The New Economic Paradigm and Reading the Future

questions.question: The new economic paradigm holds that cycles are best smoothed by:
options: Moderate, predictable demand-side policy combined with supply-side measures that raise capacity and efficiency
Maximum government spending at all times

questions.question: Which set contains LEADING indicators?
options: New manufacturing orders, building plans approved, share prices and confidence surveys

questions.question: Unemployment is a LAGGING indicator because:
options: It never changes over the cycle
Firms rehire only once recovery is certain, so it keeps rising after the trough has passed

questions.question: The weakness of EXTRAPOLATION as a forecasting technique is that:
options: It is illegal in national accounting
It assumes the future repeats the past — the assumption that fails exactly at turning points

questions.question: In the tourist town, guesthouses half-empty with nothing getting worse anymore is the:
options: Trough — the lowest point, where activity stops falling

questions.question: During the upswing, the cleaner's new wages are spent at the spaza and those takings are spent again. This climbing-feeding-climbing is:
Every room taken, no bricklayer available at any wage, prices creeping up — the town is at:
options: The peak — activity cannot rise further and prices accelerate

questions.question: The wave, the slope and the swing: in the town's story these are respectively:
options: The budget, the repo rate and the deficit
The cycle, the long-term trend, and the amplitude

questions.question: The repo rate works like a thermostat because:
options: Turning it down makes borrowing cheaper and heats up spending; turning it up makes loans pinch and cools spending
It sets the price of petrol
It changes the weather for tourism

questions.question: The rate hikes of 2022 and 2023 were the thermostat turned:
options: Up, to cool spending and slow the climb in prices

questions.question: The waiter who loses his job stops paying income tax and starts drawing UIF. This shows that:
options: The safety net is also a shock absorber — spending falls by less than the wage did, with nobody deciding anything

questions.question: "Neither lever builds a power station" means:
options: Monetary policy is stronger than fiscal policy
Electricity is not part of the economy
Power stations are built by the Reserve Bank
Demand-side tools cannot fix a supply-side constraint — cheap loans and big budgets queue money behind the outage

subtopics.title: Reading the Signs Before the Wave Turns

questions.question: Bookings made months ahead and building plans approved at the municipality are:
options: Leading indicators — actions taken today because of what people expect tomorrow

questions.question: Averaging each month's takings with its neighbours to strip out short-term noise is called:
Extrapolation "works right up until the turning point" because:
options: It projects the current path forward, and turning points are precisely where the path changes
It only applies to leading indicators

questions.question: "Narrow the amplitude, raise the trend" summarises:
options: The Keynesian rejection of all policy
A plan to abolish business cycles completely
The new paradigm — steady demand-side policy to keep swings small, plus supply-side measures to lift the long-term growth path
